doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02

title: Billie's musical family, learning piano and first blues
summary: Billie says her parents and sisters all played piano by ear, mostly in the Baptist church; she learned blues first and later decided with Edna to go into show business.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When, you might tell a little bit about your life and give D.D. a rest. When you started in music, about your family, the, did your mother and father play any instruments?
They all play piano. All of your sisters, I believe you told me before, played piano.

All played piano. All my niece's nephew plays piano. Everyone in the family is musical pianos. Yeah. Of course, they take other instruments that they wanted to learn. Some one is trombone, one is sax.
Like that, and one banjo. But they still got that piano. They still got that piano.
How long did you live in your hometown before you moved away?
I lived in my hometown. I got it before I went away. I was around 15 years old when I left my hometown. And that's when I went out.
Where did you go then? Well, I started traveling. Just traveling and playing music then?

Yeah, I was playing music. Playing music, it sure was. Who taught you on piano? Did you have lessons on piano or pick it up? None of us never had no lessons. Just picked it up. From my mother and father, that's all. That's why I accumulated that, through my mother and father.
Did you have any book when you learned or just play by ear?

Just play by ear. Anything I heard I wanted to play, I just went on and played it. And the first thing I learned how to play, I couldn't hardly talk good. I wasn't big enough to hardly make good on the piano, you know, then, because I was quite small. It was the blues. I never did love but one man in my life, he was a married man, I'd taken him from his wife. I never forget that long as I lived. That's the first thing I thought I sang in the blues. And then by, growing up, my sister Edna and I, we decided we would go out and show business.
Did you explain that, were you about the third sister or how, were the others older, how many were older than you?
Well, Sadie older than you? Sadie and Edna older and I, see. And then comes me and then come Ida, Ida's the baby girls.
Did your father or mother ever play in any bands or? No, they never did.
They just played most around the church. Played church. Which church did they play?
What kind of a church? Was it Baptist or Methodist? Baptist. Baptist.
Which church did you belong to, D.D.? Catholic, all of them.
